title: Systems Working Together
summary: Learn how connected subsystems support a data center and how one problem can affect another system.
objectives: Explain what a subsystem and dependency are.
Use observations to identify which system may be affected by a simple problem.

vocab.def: One smaller system that is part of a larger system.
A connection where one part relies on another part.
A careful process for finding what may be causing a problem.

sections.heading: A data center is a connected system
sections.body: Servers do computing, but they depend on networks, electricity, cooling, monitoring, security, and people. Each supporting area is a subsystem.

sections.heading: Problems can cross system boundaries
sections.body: A server can have power and still be unreachable if its network connection has a problem. A cooling issue can affect several servers. Good troubleshooting starts by noticing the evidence.

sections.heading: Start with safe questions
sections.body: Observe what changed, identify the affected system, and ask what information would help. Classroom troubleshooting is reasoning practice, not a direction to open equipment or perform repairs.

practice.prompt: A classroom computer turns on but cannot reach a website. Which systems could be involved: power, network, or both? Explain what you would observe first.

quiz.question: Why can one data-center subsystem affect another?
options: The subsystems depend on connected resources
Every subsystem does exactly the same job
A server never needs other systems
quiz.answer: The subsystems depend on connected resources

reflectionPrompt: Which connected system would you most like to understand better, and what evidence would help you study it?
